title: Add `user_data_dir` to `read_html_live()`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Persists Chrome's profile across sessions, so you can log in once with `mode = "visible"` and then scrape with `mode = "headless"`. Shared browsers are now keyed by mode and profile; since Chrome locks a profile to one process, requesting a different mode for the same `user_data_dir` closes the browser using the other mode. The mode-switch path isn't covered by tests since visible mode can't run on CI.

title: Add methods for saving LiveHTML pages
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Adds `$screenshot(path, css, full_page)`, `$save_pdf(path, paper, landscape, background)`, and `$save_html(path, base)` to `LiveHTML`. `$save_html()` is a static render: `<script>` elements are dropped and current form values are written into attributes. Adds jsonlite to Suggests (already imported by chromote) for decoding base64 CDP output.

title: Add LiveHTML methods for accessing downloaded resources
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Adds `$resource_list()`, `$resource_get()`, and `$resource_get_json()` to `LiveHTML`, so you can get data (e.g. JSON) that the page fetched instead of scraping the HTML generated from it.

`wait` only helps when nothing matches yet; after an action, the `url` pattern needs to be specific to the new resource.

title: Make `LiveHTML$scroll_by()` scroll the page
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Previously `scroll_by()` dispatched a mouse wheel event at (0, 0), which scrolled whatever element was under that point. The page now gets `scroll` but not `wheel` events.

Also simplifies `scroll_to()` to call `window.scrollTo()` directly, for consistency.

title: Add `clear` argument to `LiveHTML$type()`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Existing text is deleted with a real Backspace key press so the page sees normal input events. Will conflict with #495 in the `type()` signature.

title: Add `LiveHTML$close()`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Using the object after closing gives an informative error rather than attempting to respawn. This will conflict with #493 in `check_active()`; the closed check should come first.

title: Add `timeout` to `LiveHTML` interaction methods
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

`$click()`, `$press()`, `$scroll_into_view()`, `$select()`, and `$type()` previously always waited 5 seconds for the element to appear. `$download()` now also passes its `timeout` to the click.

title: Close tab when `LiveHTML` navigation fails
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Stacked on #493. Previously a failed load left an orphaned tab open in the shared browser.

title: Reopen current page when `LiveHTML` session closes
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Previously a closed tab made every subsequent call error, since `respawn()` refuses closed targets (and when it did work, it lost the URL, viewport, and user-agent override).

Only the URL is restored, so any interaction since the last navigation is lost.

title: Snapshot page in `LiveHTML$html_elements()`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Selecting 2,000 elements drops from ~2.6s to ~0.01s, and returned elements now share a tree so `xml_parent()` etc. work.

Note that CSS in `html_elements()` is now evaluated by selectr rather than Chrome, so browser-only selectors like `:has()` no longer work there, while the interaction methods still use Chrome's engine.

title: Scope `$download()` to the session's tab
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Since the live browser is shared across sessions, `$download()` previously changed download behavior for every tab and could claim a download started by another session.

title: Fix `html_table(fill)` deprecation attribution
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

The `html_table(fill)` deprecation warning blamed rvest ("likely used in the rvest package") when called on an `xml_document` or `xml_nodeset`, because those methods re-dispatch to the `xml_node` method. Spotted in the teal.widgets revdep check.

title: docs: fix a typo
description:
docs: fix a typo

Does this help?

Should I run:

```r
devtools::document()
```

title: Allow `html_form_submit(submit = FALSE)`
description:
🤖 Written by AI 🤖

Lets you submit a form without including any button, which is useful for forms submitted by JavaScript when a field changes. Uses `FALSE` rather than the `NA` suggested in the issue since it reads more naturally as "no button".

Fixes #439.

title: Improve `LiveHTML` element lookup and waiting
description:
* Cache the document root node id in a new internal `DocumentRoot` R6 class, invalidated on `DOM.documentUpdated`, instead of calling `DOM.getDocument` on every lookup.
* Retry `querySelectorAll` once with a fresh root if the cached id is stale.
* Rewrite `wait_for_selector()` to wait in-page with a `MutationObserver`, so it resolves as soon as the element appears and errors immediately on invalid selectors.
* `wait_for_selector()` now returns only the first matching node, fixing `$click()`, `$type()`, `$press()`, and `$scroll_into_view()` when a selector matches multiple elements.

title: Add `LiveHTML$download()`
description:
Adds a `$download(css, dir = tempdir(), timeout = 30)` method to `LiveHTML`. It clicks an element that triggers a download, waits for Chrome to report that the download has finished, and returns the path to the saved file.

* Uses `Browser.setDownloadBehavior()` plus download-event callbacks driven by `later::run_now()`. Waiting for one event at a time with `wait_for()` promises missed the final event, because Chrome sends several progress events in quick succession.
* `later` is added to Suggests; it's always installed with chromote.

Tested offline with a `data:` URL fixture.

Fixes #437.

title: Preserve spaces between inline elements in html_text2()
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖 ## Problem `html_text2()` dropped spaces between inline elements when the whitespace lived in its own node, e.g. `a b` returned `"ab"` instead of `"a b"` (#372). The same happened for `a b`. ## Cause Each inline child was collapsed independently by `collapse_whitespace()`, which trims leading/trailing whitespace, so whitespace-only nodes became `""` and were dropped. Per the CSS whitespace rules that `innerText` follows, whitespace should only be removed at line boundaries; between text on the same line it collapses to a single space. ## Fix - `PaddedText` gains a pending-space mechanism: `add_space()` records whitespace and the space is only emitted if more text follows on the same line. It is discarded at line boundaries (margins, `
`, ``, ``) and at the start/end of output. - New `add_collapsed_text()` helper detects leading/trailing whitespace on raw text and routes it through `add_space()`. - `
` content bypasses this so its literal whitespace is preserved.

Fixes #372

title: Add public `LiveHTML$wait_for()` method
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖

`read_html_live()` waits for Chrome's load event, but JS-heavy pages often render content *after* that event fires, so `html_elements()` can return nothing unless the user adds an arbitrary `Sys.sleep()` (#428).

This PR exposes the existing private `wait_for_selector()` polling logic as a public `LiveHTML$wait_for(css, timeout = 5)` method, so users can wait for specific content to appear:

```r
page <- read_html_live("https://www.scopus.com/sourceid/21100258853")
page$wait_for("td:nth-child(1) div")
```

It errors informatively if the element doesn't appear within `timeout` seconds. Includes a new `dynamic.html` test fixture, tests (including a snapshot of the timeout error), and a NEWS bullet.

Fixes #428.

title: Add `html_table2()`
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖 Adds `html_table2()`, which works just like `html_table()` but uses `html_text2()` to extract cell text, so `
` elements become newlines and cell text more closely resembles what you see in a browser. The shared parsing logic is refactored into an internal `table_parse()` helper, and `table_fill()` gains a `text_fun` argument. `html_table2()` drops the deprecated `fill` argument. Fixes #361

title: Fix file uploads in form submission
description:
Setting a file field to `httr::upload_file()` in `html_form_set()` silently broke uploads: `submission_build_values()` coerced every value with `as.character()`, turning the upload object into strings of its path and MIME type. httr then sent them as plain text fields instead of a multipart file part, so the server received no file.

Fixes #320

title: Remove functions deprecated in 1.0.0 and stabilise read_html_live()
description:
Advance the lifecycle of deprecations made in rvest 1.0.0:

- Removes deprecated functions: `set_values()`, `submit_form()`, `xml_tag()`, `xml_node()`, `xml_nodes()`, `back()`, `forward()`, `jump_to()`, `follow_link()`, `html_session()`, `guess_encoding()`, and `repair_encoding()`.
- `html_node()`/`html_nodes()` remain as superseded (not removed) due to wide usage.
- Removes the deprecated `fill` argument to `html_table()` (all methods, including session and `LiveHTML`).
- Removes the experimental badge from `read_html_live()` and `LiveHTML`.
- Drops the now-unused `lifecycle::deprecated` import, updates tests/snapshots, and adds a NEWS bullet.

Full test suite passes (206 PASS, 1 unrelated pre-existing skip).

title: Document that `html_elements()` only matches descendants
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖

Clarifies in the `html_element()`/`html_elements()` docs that when applied to a node or node set, only *descendants* of the input are searched — the input nodes themselves are never matched. This behavior is by design (it makes recursive document traversal safe), but it surprised users in #382 when CSS selectors failed to match top-level nodes in a node set.

Fixes #382.

title: Default missing form `action` to document URL
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖

Per the HTML5 spec, a form without an `action` attribute submits to the document's URL. `html_form()` now implements this default, so forms without an `action` can be submitted without manually setting `form$action` (h/t @epiben's suggestion in the issue).

When the document has no URL (e.g. HTML parsed from a string), the existing `html_form_submit()` error is preserved, since there is no URL to fall back on.

Fixes #319.

title: Support httr2 responses in read_html()
description:
Adds a `read_html.httr2_response` S3 method so `read_html()` accepts an httr2 response directly. The method checks the response status, extracts the raw body, and parses it with the response URL as `base_url` so relative links resolve correctly. httr2 is added to Suggests, with tests covering parsing and the document URL.

Fixes #406.

title: Only submit checked checkboxes and radio buttons
description:
`submission_build_values()` previously submitted the `value` of every checkbox and radio button regardless of checked state, so forms went out with every box effectively checked.

* `html_form_submit()` now skips unchecked checkboxes/radio buttons (per the HTML spec they are not successful controls); a checked one with no `value` attribute submits the default `"on"`.
* `html_form_set()` now toggles the checked state for checkbox/radio fields: pass a character vector of values to check, which also handles radio groups and checkbox sets correctly. Setting a value that doesn't exist errors with the possible values.

Fixes #316.

title:
Convert nested
to newline in html_text2()
description:
`html_text2()` ignored a `
` nested inside an inline element, so ```r html_text2(minimal_html("

line 1
line 2

")) #> "line 1line 2" ``` `html_text_inline()` only looked at the direct children of the block and took `xml_text()` of each, which never contains the `
` of a nested element. When the block contains a `
`, child elements are now replaced by their own contents (recursively), so a nested `
` becomes `"\n"` like a direct one. Blocks without a `
` take the same path as before, and output for them is unchanged. Comments behave as before: a direct-child comment still contributes its text, and a comment nested in an element is still dropped. Closes #351

title: Fix swapped outerHTML/localName in LiveHTML element parsing
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖

`LiveHTML$html_elements()` calls JS that returns `[localName, outerHTML]`, but then read `json[[1]]` as the HTML and `json[[2]]` as the tag name. This made `xml2::read_html()` treat tag names like "head" or "p" as file paths, erroring with 'does not exist in current working directory' for essentially every element selection.

Introduced in #470. This PR swaps the indices so `json[[2]]` (outerHTML) is parsed and `json[[1]]` (localName) is used for the xpath.

No NEWS bullet since this fixes a bug introduced in the current dev version.

title: Add `timeout` argument to `read_html_live()`
description:
Adds a `timeout` argument to `read_html_live()` (default 10s, matching chromote's current default) that is passed to `Page$loadEventFired()`.

Fixes #427.

title: Fix `LiveHTML` selection of `<html>`, `<head>`, and `<body>`
description:
`html_elements()` now parses each element individually and locates it by the browser-reported `localName`, rather than concatenating everything and assuming a fixed depth. This fixes printing, which previously showed the children of `<head>` and `<body>`.

Fixes #396.

title: Add `method` argument to `LiveHTML$click()`
description:
`LiveHTML$click()` gains a `method` argument:

* `method = "mouse"` (default) keeps the existing behavior of simulating a real mouse click.
* `method = "js"` calls JavaScript's `element.click()` directly, which works on hidden or zero-sized elements (e.g. invisible map markers), at the cost of only firing the `click` event.

Clicking an element that can't be clicked with the mouse (no layout box) now errors with a message suggesting `method = "js"`, instead of surfacing a raw CDP error.

Fixes #431

title: `read_html_live()` errors when page fails to load
description:
🤖 Generated by AI 🤖

Previously, `read_html_live()` ignored the result of `Page$navigate()` and just waited for the load event, which never fires when navigation fails — so bad URLs hung forever. Now it:

* errors if Chrome reports an `errorText` (e.g. `https://doeasdfsdafastnexist.com` → `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`)
* catches chromote protocol errors for invalid URLs (e.g. `".//"` → `Cannot navigate to invalid URL`) and re-raises them with `read_html_live()` as the call instead of chromote's internal `callback()`
* validates that `url` is a single non-empty string before launching anything

All errors surface quickly as `Failed to load <url>: ...`.

title: Add `LiveHTML$select()` for `<select>` dropdowns
description:
Fixes #411. Adds a new `$select(css, value, text)` method to `LiveHTML` for selecting options in `` element (`"p" selects a

element, not a

title: Hide automated-browser tells in `read_html_live()`
description:
## Summary

`read_html_live()` now hides common tells that reveal an automated browser, and gains arguments to control how the browser presents itself:

- Chrome is launched with `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` and `--headless=new`, which removes `navigator.webdriver` and populates `navigator.languages`, `navigator.plugins`, and `window.chrome` correctly (verified empirically on Chrome 153 — no JS patching is needed).
- The user agent is derived from the real `navigator.userAgent` with `HeadlessChrome` replaced, so the platform and version are always correct. (The old hardcoded UA claimed Chrome/121 on macOS regardless of the actual browser.)
- New `mode = c("headless", "visible")` argument: `"visible"` opens a browser window, useful when debugging scraping scripts.
- New `view = c("desktop", "mobile")` argument: desktop (1280×800) is now the default, fixing the previous mobile-like 992×1323 viewport; `"mobile"` uses a 390×844 viewport with chromote's mobile emulation.

Implementation notes:

- A new `stealth_session()` helper launches a dedicated Chrome rather than the shared default chromote object, so rvest can control launch flags without mutating the user's global chromote state. The browser is closed via `session$parent$close()` in `finalize()`.
- The existing scroll test expectation was updated for the new 800px-tall desktop viewport.

Fixes #407. Fixes #438.

title: fix #417
description:
I ran into #417 today on a new system. I figured out it happens when chromote is installed only after attaching rvest (which is not unlikely as the user is asked to install it when it's missing):

``` r
rlang::is_installed("chromote")
#> [1] FALSE
library(rvest)
install.packages("chromote")
#> Installing package into '/home/johannes/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5'
#> (as 'lib' is unspecified)
sess <- rvest::read_html_live('https://www.forbes.com/top-colleges/')
message('curosr at ', sess$get_scroll_position()$y)
#> Error in new_chromote && !self$session$is_active(): invalid 'x' type in 'x && y'
```

<sup>Created on 2025-11-17 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

The issue is that in this case, `new_chromote` was previously only assigned locally.

title: `read_html_live()` errors with "invalid 'x' type in 'x && y'" when chromote is installed after rvest is loaded
description:
Found this during my most recent [ry](https://github.com/sims1253/ry) audit

## Summary

When `chromote` is **not** installed at the time `rvest` is loaded, the
package-level `new_chromote` flag is left at its initial value of `NULL`
instead of being set to `FALSE`. Any subsequent `LiveHTML` operation that
calls `private$check_active()` then evaluates
`if (new_chromote && !self$session$is_active())`, and `NULL && <logical>`
raises an error at runtime:

```
Error: invalid 'x' type in 'x && y'
```

This is reachable in practice when a user installs `chromote` *after*
loading `rvest` in the same R session (e.g. they load rvest first, then
realize they need live scraping and install chromote, then call
`read_html_live()`).

## reprex

```r
# In a fresh R session where rvest is installed but chromote is NOT:
library(rvest)

# ...then install chromote later in the same session:
install.packages("chromote")

# Now any LiveHTML interaction that reaches check_active() fails:
sess <- read_html_live("https://rvest.tidyverse.org/articles/starwars.html")
sess$view()
#> Error: invalid 'x' type in 'x && y'
```

(The error is thrown from `LiveHTML$check_active()` at
`if (new_chromote && !self$session$is_active())` in `R/live.R`.)

## Root cause

In `R/zzz.R`, the package binding is initialised to `NULL`:

```r
new_chromote <- NULL

.onLoad <- function(...) {
  if (is_installed("chromote")) {
    new_chromote <<- utils::packageVersion("chromote") >= "0.1.2.9000"  # <<- : ok
  } else {
    new_chromote <- FALSE                                                # <- : BUG (local only)
  }
  invisible()
}
```

The `if` branch uses the super-assignment `<<-`, which correctly updates the
package-level binding. The `else` branch uses a **local** `<-`, which only
creates a local variable inside `.onLoad` and never reaches the package
binding. When chromote is absent at load time, `new_chromote` therefore stays
`NULL`. Later, `new_chromote && ...` evaluates `NULL && x`, which R rejects
(`NULL` is not a valid length-1 logical operand for `&&`):

```r
NULL && TRUE
#> Error: invalid 'x' type in 'x && y'
```

title: Fix `read_html_live()` xpath with single quotes
description:
Fixes #435.

Two bugs in `LiveHTML$find_nodes()`:

1. The xpath was interpolated into the JavaScript inside single quotes, so an xpath containing `'x'` broke the JS string literal. The xpath is now embedded via a `js_string()` helper that escapes backslashes, double quotes, and newlines, so both quote styles work.
2. The xpath branch never called `DOM$getDocument()` before `requestNode()`/`resolveNode()`, so on a fresh session the DOM agent had no document tree and node resolution failed with "No node with given id found". It only worked when a CSS query ran first. The xpath branch now calls `private$root_id()` first.

title: LiveHTML: use dynamic root ID
description:
Fixes #405.

I discussed with @schloerke, and this is very much his suggestion / solution.

- The document root ID should always be retrieved dynamically rather than stored within the R6 object as it's subject to change (as we've discovered in #405).

- In Shinytest2, there is an [equivalent helper](https://github.com/rstudio/shinytest2/blob/4e6de2a46e05698b4fa943487ffb66c7d8821021/R/chromote-methods.R#L202C1-L208C1) to retrieve the root ID.

- This PR makes `private$root_id` a function, so it is now always called as `private$root_id()`. This ensures that we never have a stale root id.

Should check cleanly after #445 is merged.

FYI @jonthegeek this is a simpler version of what you were attempting in #413 - you also had the right idea with `private$refresh_root()`.

@hadley for your review, thanks!

title: Wait in click()
description:
Closes #405.

I tried to make this automatic, and got it working some of the time, but I couldn't find a way to detect that something *might* change, and thus wait in that situation. I tried to make it as clear as possible for users to be able to fix this. Once a strategy is agreed on, the same strategy should probably be applied to other methods.

An approach I worked on but failed to finalize would be to either wait for a `loadEventFired()` event *or* time out (probably after a relatively brief time, and only if no events occur in that window, or something along those lines). I couldn't find a clean way to check if anything is in progress and thus wait if so; if we're waiting for a loadEventFired that never fires, we'll introduced a new error for many click events.

I also tried adding `private$refresh_root()` as a callback on `loadEventFired()`, which might be a useful approach but it still doesn't solve the issue of users not waiting for that to occur before executing their next step.

I like this better than status quo (since it makes it *possible* to deal with these situations), but I'm not sure that it's quite there yet.

title: S7 in rvest
description:
Closes #414.

Converted some S3 classes to S7 in `form.R` and `session.R.`

**Notable changes:**

-  The S3 implementation of `rvest_field` allowed for dots to be passed. I noted that the dots were only ever used to pass one (optional) argument, `options`; as such, I added `options` as a new property to the S7 implementation but did not include a way to pass the dots when creating a `rvest_field.` That is an easy fix if needed.
- Adjusted tests to match S7 syntax and the like.
- Bumped Roxygen to 7.3.2.

**Issues**

- The "basic session process works as expected" test fails locally. I get the same (incorrect) test output with the original S3 implementation cloned from Github though. I get `Size: 821905` instead of `Size: 20707` as the snapshot asserts. I think this is an error with the test?
- No documentation for any S7 pecularities.

title: Add `convert` arg to html_table() to control whether to run conversion or not.
description:
Fix #311 

I chose `convert` as the argument name because it's used some of tidyr's functions.

``` r
library(tibble)

d <- tibble(code = c("001", "002", "101", "102"),
            label = c("apple", "banana", "lemon", "orange"))

devtools::load_all("~/repo/rvest/")
#> Loading rvest

table_html <- knitr::kable(d, format = "html")
table_html <- as.character(table_html)

h <- table_html %>% 
  read_html()


html_table(h)
#> [[1]]
#> # A tibble: 4 x 2
#>    code label 
#>   <int> <chr> 
#> 1     1 apple 
#> 2     2 banana
#> 3   101 lemon 
#> 4   102 orange

html_table(h, convert = FALSE)
#> [[1]]
#> # A tibble: 4 x 2
#>   code  label 
#>   <chr> <chr> 
#> 1 001   apple 
#> 2 002   banana
#> 3 101   lemon 
#> 4 102   orange
```

title: Simplify and fix colspan and rowspan filling in html_table
description:
When reading a HTML table containing cells spanning multiple rows, `html_table` may behave incorrectly - I have set up a [repository](https://github.com/jaanos/rvest-table-fill) illustrating the issue. This pull request fixes the problem, at least for well-formed tables:

* If not all `<tr>`s span the same number of columns, the total number of cells is compared to the product of the number of rows and the maximal span to determine whether `fill = TRUE` is needed. The current checks (comparing against the sums of rowspans and colspans) never succeed.
* When filling the matrix, vectors are maintained indicating how many cells to the right and below the current cell spans. This allows skipping the cells spanning from previous rows, thus emulating how browsers display tables.

This should work for all tables in which the total number of cells in each row (including cells from previous rows spanning down to the current row) is constant, no cell spans below the last `<tr>`, and cells do not overlap (i.e., multicolumn cells do not span over a range of columns containing multirow cells spanning from previous rows).

* A malformed table may have more columns than the maximal sum of colspans in a `<tr>` (in a well-formed table, the maximum is achieved in the first row). This patch silently drops any cells that would fall outside the output matrix. If issuing a warning or even an error would be preferable, I can change that.
* Similarly, any multirow cells spanning below the last `<tr>` will be cut at the bottom of the table (but here, no data loss can occur).
* If there are overlapping cells, data from the cell appearing later in the table (i.e., beginning in a row closer to the bottom and in a column closer to the left) is used at points of overlap.
* It may happen that a malformed table passes the colspan or number of cells test even with `fill = FALSE`, thus keeping `NA`s in shorter rows.

Detecting the actual number of columns would of course be possible, but would require another pass through the cells (or adding columns on-the-fly), which might slow down the function.

Anyway, using this patch, the table from the repository linked above can be read correctly without using `fill = TRUE`.

title: Unlist request values of length > 1 before submitting form.
description:
Suppose I want to submit a form with a `<select>` that allows multiple selection, such as [this one](http://www.w3schools.com/tags/tryit.asp?filename=tryhtml_select_multiple). I can do it with `rvest`, but it fails if I want to select more than one `<option>` : 

``` r
library(rvest)
s <- html_session("http://www.w3schools.com/tags")
forms <- s %>% 
  jump_to('tryit.asp?filename=tryhtml_select_multiple') %>% 
  read_html() %>% html_form()
f <- set_values(forms[[1]], cars = c("volvo", "saab"))
submit_form(s,f)
```

Which gives  

```
Error in vapply(elements, encode, character(1)) : 
  values must be length 1,
 but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 2
```

One solution seems to `unlist` the list of request values from this : 

``` r
$cars
[1] "volvo" "saab" 
```

to this : 

``` r
$cars
[1] "volvo"

$cars
[1] "saab"
```

That is the goal of this PR, which checks if one of the request values has a length > 1, and if it is TRUE, unlist these values while preserving original names.

title: Improved checkboxes and radio buttons handling
description:
Improved checkboxes and radio buttons handling in set_values and submit_request.

Namely, now set_values turns the 'checked' field (in the form$fields list) to "true" when the value is the correct one. Accordingly, submit_request acknowledge the checkbox values only when 'checked' is set to "true" (for radio buttons, other options are set to "false").

This submission also allows better handling of checkbox forms where the same name is used for multiple "checks" and different values should be set altogether (e.g. "name"="foo_value1", "name"="foo_value2", etc.).

Code has been tested on several online forms with no apparent issue, e.g.
- wikipedia advanced search for testing forms with separate checkbox names,
- IMDB advanced search for forms with checkboxes sharing the same name for multiple options.

NOTE: I tried to follow Hadley's code style, but there might be space for further cleanup: please let me know whether anything is necessary before accepting the pull request or if you can take care of such thing...

title: Add functions to work with HTML classes
description:
These functions handle adding, removing, and getting HTML classes.
These functions handle some of the annoyances of HTML classes, including converting to and from the space-separated string format in the attribute to a character vector, ordering of classnames, and duplication of classnames.

-   `html_classes`: returns HTML classes as character vector.
-   `html_classes<-` and `html_set_classes`: sets the classes of a HTML element.
-   `html_remove_classes`: removes one or more classes from a HTML element.
-   `html_add_classes`: adds one or more classes to a HTML element.
-   `html_has_classes`: checks whether an element has a HTML class (or multiple HTML classes).

title: add form input images as valid submit buttons
description:
The HTML spec allows forms to use `<input type="image">` elements as the submit button, but currently rvest doesn't recognize such elements as form submission targets.

Example:

``` r
library(rvest)

entry_page <- html_session("http://dl.acm.org")

search <-
  entry_page %>% 
  html_nodes("form") %>% 
  .[[1]] %>% 
  html_form() %>% 
  set_values(
    query = "programming"
  )

entry_page %>% 
  submit_form(search, "Go")    # no element found

entry_page %>% 
  submit_form(search)      # error: subscript out of bounds
```

title: Additional args to be passed to `httr::GET()`
description:
Hi Hadley,

this is my first pull request ever - so please don't bite ;-)
## Reason for modification

I needed to pass along altered user agent information for the underlying `GET` request in `html()`
## Actual modification

In order to avoid this

```
require("httr")
content(GET(<url>,  user_agent("Mozilla/5.0")))
```

I modified `html()`: it now accepts `...` to pass additional arguments along to `httr::GET()` for this to work

```
html(<url>, encoding = NULL, user_agent("Mozilla/5.0")
```

As making use of `...` involves the need to explicitly specify `encoding = NULL` in calls to `html()` (unless making `...` the second argument in `html()`), you might want to go with the second (commented-out) implementation of `html()` featuring an actual formal argument `httr_config` for the things to pass to `httr::GET()`.
## Unit test

I also added a short unit test for a German website that throws a `403` error for the default user agent.

Best regards and thanks for the cool package!

title: fix demo due to webpage change
description:
The demo `trpadvisor.R` seems not to work for me in the last line. All previous scraping lines works fine but `review` gets 19 elements instead of 10.

``` rconsole
> data.frame(id, quote, rating, date, review, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>% View()
Error in data.frame(id, quote, rating, date, review, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 10, 19
```

I visit the webpage and found that `.partial_entry` will not only select review but also their responses. As a result, `review` may have more than 10 entries (19 entries currently). `.entry .partial_entry` selector will fix the problem by only selecting reviews.
